description: Workspace frontmatter validation CORE PROFILE (mechanisms only, workspace-agnostic). Declares HOW frontmatter is validated as data — the cardinality vocabulary, the ordered tag-rule cascade with its exact violation codes/fields/message templates, the general conditional `rule_sets` mechanism, and the required-field / description-cap / file-class / exempt mechanisms — WITHOUT any concrete namespace names, caps, or globs (those live in an extension pack that sets `extends: core@2`). `core@2` is a BREAKING change from `core@1`: the `core@1` `report`-named construct is removed and generalized into the `rule_sets` `{match, apply}` mechanism (there is no report-named branch anywhere). INPUTS: an extension pack (concrete vocab) + one file's parsed frontmatter (`{fields, tags[], path}`). OUTPUT: an ordered list of violations `{code, field, message}` plus a derived `file_class`, byte-identical for identical input. INVARIANTS: the `violation_cascade` array is order-significant and any interpreter MUST iterate it in array order so emitted code+field sequences are stable; every namespace/required-field/rule-set iteration follows the DECLARED array order; no LLM participates in validation.

instance_shape.fields: map of top-level frontmatter keys to values; a field required by the pack counts as present whether declared top-level or nested under the `workspace:` wrapper (Skills/Agents/Rules), per CLAUDE.md frontmatter table and schema.py REQUIRED_FIELDS comment (schema.py:60-62)
instance_shape.tags: list of raw tag strings; each meaningful tag is `namespace:value`; non-string or colon-less entries are dropped before any namespace rule runs (schema.py:107-119 tag_namespaces)
instance_shape.path: repo-root-relative POSIX path of the file (drives file_class classification and exempt matching)

at_least_one.meaning: namespace must appear one or more times

optional.meaning: namespace may appear zero or more times; still subject to parent-dependency and conditional rule-set rules
optional.source: CLAUDE.md Tagging Strategy — namespaces marked optional/❌

authorship.meaning: per-field fix-tier boundary read from the schema (not hardcoded) by `navigator fix` (M4.P3.T2). `machine_derivable` = a deterministic Tier-1 repair can produce/stamp it; `human_authored` = only the operator-gated Tier-2 model turn may author it. `file_class` is a derived attribute (machine_derivable), not an authored field.
authorship.source: NEW mechanism (build-plan M2.P1.T1 declaration list + M4.P3.T2 fix tiers); see DIVERGENCES.md

required_fields.meaning: the pack supplies an ordered array of `{field, authorship, source}`; each listed field must be present (top-level or under `workspace:`). A missing field emits one violation.
required_fields.source: schema.py:60-62 REQUIRED_FIELDS (field tuple); code string + message template pinned to the live emitter frontmatter.py:360-362 (`MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`, message `required field '{field}:' is missing`). Confirmed against live, not assumed. See DIVERGENCES.md D5.

description_caps.meaning: the pack supplies a map `file_class -> max description length` (character count). The `description` field is capped by the file's derived `file_class`; a class absent from the map is uncapped (NOTE: the pack MUST supply a cap for every file_class its `file_class` mechanism can derive — the live emitter indexes the cap map directly). Exceeding the cap (len strictly greater) emits one violation.
description_caps.message: description is {length} chars, over the {file_class} cap of {cap}
description_caps.source: NEW mechanism — CLAUDE.md frontmatter table description-cap classes (context ≤350, skill ≤500, agent ≤750). Absent from schema.py, but LIVE in the emitter frontmatter.py:364-374: code `DESCRIPTION_OVER_CAP`, char-count `len(description) > DESCRIPTION_CAPS[file_class]`, message `description is {len} chars, over the {file_class.value} cap of {cap}`. Code string + message template pinned to live. See DIVERGENCES.md D2.

namespaces.meaning: the pack supplies an ORDER-SIGNIFICANT array of `{name, cardinality, parents?, type?}`. Array order IS the iteration order for every cascade phase that scans namespaces. `parents` = ordered list of namespaces that must co-occur when this namespace is used.
namespaces.source: CLAUDE.md Tagging Strategy namespaces (cardinality/parents); per-namespace `type` drives downstream range-eligibility

rule_sets.meaning: the pack supplies an ORDER-SIGNIFICANT array of general conditional rule-sets `{match:{namespace,value}, apply:{require_namespaces[], forbidden_unless_matched[], value_formats[{namespace,regex,message}]}}`. A file MATCHES a rule-set when its tags carry `match.namespace:match.value`. On a matching file, each `require_namespaces` entry must be present and each `value_formats` entry's tags must satisfy its `regex` (a `date_interval`-typed namespace is additionally calendar-checked). On a NON-matching file, each `forbidden_unless_matched` namespace must be ABSENT. The report axis is one instance (match `type:report`); this mechanism has no report-named branch.
rule_sets.source: Generalizes the retired `core@1` report construct (trigger/required/period + the `report_only` namespace flag) into one `{match, apply}` mechanism

file_class.meaning: the pack supplies `{rules:[{class, match:{glob}}], default}`. Rules are evaluated in array order against the repo-root-relative POSIX path (glob per fnmatch semantics, `*` spans `/`); the FIRST matching rule wins; if none match, `default` is used. The derived class selects the `description_caps` entry. No violation code — classification is an input to other checks.
file_class.source: NEW mechanism — derived from CLAUDE.md description-cap classes (context/skill/agent). Absent from schema.py. See DIVERGENCES.md for classification logic.

exempt.meaning: the pack supplies `{filenames[], dir_components[], path_globs[]}`. A repo-root-relative path is exempt from the frontmatter-completeness scan if: its basename is in `filenames`; OR any of its path components is in `dir_components`; OR its POSIX path matches any `path_globs` entry (fnmatch, `*` spans `/`, anchored as written). Exempt files are skipped entirely (no required-field or tag checks).

violation_cascade.iterate: namespaces where cardinality == 'singleton', in pack-declared array order
namespaces where cardinality == 'at_least_one', in pack-declared array order
namespaces that declare a non-empty `parents`, in pack-declared array order; for each, iterate its `parents` in listed order

emit.message: '{child}:' tag requires a '{parent}:' tag, which is missing

violation_cascade.action: for each rule-set, matched = (the `rule_sets[].match.namespace` group contains a tag whose value equals `rule_sets[].match.value`)
violation_cascade.source: General {match, apply} rule-set detection (generalizes the retired report trigger)

violation_cascade.iterate: each rule-set (pack-declared order); on a NON-matching file, each `apply.forbidden_unless_matched` namespace in listed order

emit.message: '{namespace}:' tag is only valid on {match} files

violation_cascade.source: Generalizes the retired report_only-misuse phase; `{match}` renders as the rule-set's `namespace:value`

violation_cascade.iterate: each rule-set (pack-declared order); on a MATCHING file, each `apply.require_namespaces` entry in listed order

emit.message: {match} requires a '{namespace}:' tag, which is missing

violation_cascade.source: Generalizes the retired report_required phase; `{match}` renders as the rule-set's `namespace:value`

violation_cascade.iterate: each rule-set (pack-declared order); on a MATCHING file, each `apply.value_formats` entry, each raw tag in its `namespace` group in file order

emit.when: tag value does NOT match the value_format `regex` (or, for a `date_interval` namespace, is not a real calendar interval)
emit.message: rendered from the matching rule-set's `apply.value_formats[].message` (pack-supplied, format-specific); this `message` field is documentation only and is not rendered

violation_cascade.source: Generalizes the retired report_period_format phase; the format wording lives with the pack's value_format rule, the code lives here

independent_checks.note: Run outside the tag cascade (schema.py keeps completeness separate from tag_rule_violations). Relative ordering vs the tag cascade is consumer-defined; each check's OWN iteration order is the pack-declared field order. Message templates for the two emitting checks live on their `mechanisms.*` entries (`required_fields.message`, `description_caps.message`) — an interpreter renders those, so its output is byte-identical to the other interpreter's.
independent_checks.exempt_gate: if `exempt` matches the path, skip required_fields + description_cap + all tag-cascade checks for this file
independent_checks.required_fields: emit MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD (field={field}, message=`mechanisms.required_fields.message`) per absent pack `required_fields` entry, in declared order
independent_checks.file_class_classification: derive file_class from path (input to description_cap; never emits)

codes.meaning: a required tag namespace (singleton, at_least_one, or a rule-set's require_namespaces) is absent
a singleton namespace appears more than once
a child namespace is used without a required parent namespace
a namespace a rule-set forbids outside its match (forbidden_unless_matched) appears on a non-matching file; code string retained for verdict-parity with pre-generalization output
a rule-set value_format check failed for a tag on a matching file; code string retained for verdict-parity with pre-generalization output
a required top-level frontmatter field is absent (checked outside the tag cascade)
codes.source: schema.py:60-62 (field tuple) + live emitter frontmatter.py:362; code string CONFIRMED against live. See DIVERGENCES.md D5.

codes.meaning: the `description` field exceeds the character cap for the file's file_class
codes.source: NEW mechanism vs schema.py, but CONFIRMED against the live emitter frontmatter.py:370 (`DESCRIPTION_OVER_CAP`). See DIVERGENCES.md D2.
